steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Do I speak into this? Hello? Hello!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: There's no need to smack it, Mr. Humus. We've set it up for you.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Just an old habit from working on my gadgets. Sometimes there's a loose part so you have to smack 'em to get 'em to work.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Well, you shouldn't have to worry about that here at the exhibition. It's being sponsored by the top tech firms in Trimounts.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (I can't exactly tell her I was being cheap so I used a bunch of second-hand parts...)

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Oh, right... did you have a question?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Yes, getting back on topic... Your participation here has drawn a lot of attention. Many people are exceptionally... curious, about your experiences and what you've made.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Well, then I should introduce the gadgets I have with me here!

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: First, this automatic clothes hanger. We've all forgotten about clothes we left out to dry, right? And sometimes they just get dirty again.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: So I modified this hanger to fold up your clothes once it senses they're dry enough, and then this device down here tosses 'em into the wardrobe.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Like that!

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Whoops, it caught your camera? Sorry, let me recalibrate it and try again.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: There's a long story behind this hanger. I made it to help the elderly and disabled—

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Ahem... the demonstration can wait, Mr. Humus. I have a few other questions for you first.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: I noticed you used the word 'modify' to describe your product, rather than 'invent,' like everyone else.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Did I? I said 'modify'?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Yes, you did. What I wanted to ask is: Did you get permission from the patent holder before modifying it?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Huh? I bought them as a pack at the supermarket for ten bucks.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Did you now?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: I see you didn't even consider that before 'modifying' your product.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: I-I guess I didn't...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Does your background have anything to do with your lack of awareness of intellectual property rights?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: W-What does that have to do with anything? They were just ordinary clothes hangers!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: In Trimounts, there can be extraordinary value in the most ordinary things, Mr. Humus.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Er... you're right! Absolutely. I agree.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: ...Then shouldn't you respect the rights of the patent holder?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: I-I've never had to deal with that kind of stuff...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Would it be correct to assume that you have virtually no understanding of patents because of your years of penal service on the frontier?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: I... I mean, I know what they are, at least...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Then do you mean to say that you do understand patents, but intentionally—

spans.text: Then do you mean to say that you

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Excuse me, ma'am, but I have urgent business with this big fellow here.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Oh... very well.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Should I come back to finish the interview later? I haven't said everything I wanted to.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: (Whisper) Just go! Don't you understand? She just wants to tear you apart.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: It wasn't that bad. It was nothing compared to the sort of stuff you hear all the time on the frontier.

spans.text: bad. It was nothing compared to the sort of stuff you hear all the time on the frontier.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: You're just... Never mind.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Are you Mr. Humus? It's such an honor to meet you. Chris talks about you all the time.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Let me introduce you to my university professor. I sent him the files on the stuff you made at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: A professor? Oh my god, I'm so excited to meet someone so intellectual!

steps.name: MC
steps.text: No need to be humble, sir. I looked through what Chris sent me, and was amazed at the creativity they demonstrated.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Aw, that was just some scrap I threw together. But you can see my latest stuff at my display.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: No need to rush, Mr. Humus, I'll be here all day. But there's something I should tell you first.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Well, now you're scaring me. Where I'm from, that's what people say when they're about to deliver bad news.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Hahaha, quite the opposite, my friend!

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Although there were more than a few rough edges in what I've seen of your work, company management was flabbergasted by some of the optimizations you made.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Flabber-what now...?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: (Whisper) They were amazed.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Aw, shucks...

steps.name: MC
steps.text: We've had an eye out for new ways to conserve and recycle resources, and your energy-saving module is precisely what we're looking for.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: So you want to...?

steps.name: MC
steps.text: We want to help you continue to improve the module and apply it to our products. You will, of course, be appropriately compensated. What do you think?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: How could I say no to that?! Getting recognized for my work is a dream come true, not to mention you're a friend of Chris.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Excellent. I like people who are easy to do business with.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Guess I better jot down all the thoughts and experiences I had on the way. Wouldn't wanna embarrass myself at the presentation, after all.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Regarding that... there's another tiny matter I must discuss with you.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: I'm all ears!

steps.name: MC
steps.text: We'd like to ask you to remain behind the scenes, and allow... others to go public with this technology.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: But why? I'm the one who made it. Would anyone else even know how to describe it?

steps.name: MC
steps.text: I'm simply saying it would be announced under somebody else's name. You won't be required to present anything. But don't worry, you will receive full compensation.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: But I wanted to talk about my experience inventing it... All the fun stuff that went into it.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: What I mean is... we would like to separate your identity from your work.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: You mean people'll use the stuff I make, but won't know it was me?

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Does that really matter? You'll have your money.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: I'm not so sure about this, prof. All the credit would go to the one who lent their name to it.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Well, we have to think about the company's image. Mr. Humus's past is a little... complicated, after all.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Hey! What's that supposed to—
Humus raises his voice, as though someone just stepped on his toes.
He then realizes that everyone in the room has their eyes on him.
Seeing everyone keep their distance and avert their gazes, Humus swallows what he was about to say.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Don't judge people by their cover, prof. I've spent a lot of time with Humus this past year, and I guarantee you he's not that kind of guy!

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Chris...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Not to mention he was imprisoned for a crime he didn't commit.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Pats the engineer's shoulder)

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Thanks for having my back, bro, but there's no need to get mad. I'm sure your professor didn't mean it like that.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Yes, there's no need to get agitated, Chris.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: This decision was made out of purely practical considerations. I assure you I have nothing against Mr. Humus himself.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Well, sir, I'm glad you think so highly of my ability, and if you're willing to buy, I'm willing to sell. But there are a lot of folks here. How 'bout we find some time to talk after the exhibition?

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Certainly. It was a pleasure meeting you. We'll speak later.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Humus...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Thanks, bro. I'll buy you lunch once I've got the cash. Just keep it cheap.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Hmm... This wasn't what I had in mind when Chris said there'd be free food here.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: How am I supposed to fill my belly with snacks the size of my fingernail?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Excuse me, you got any meat?

steps.name: Exhibition Staff
steps.text: We have meatballs with berry sauce right over there, sir.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Not that tiny stuff. Anything bigger?

steps.name: Exhibition Staff
steps.text: I'm sorry, sir, but we're only serving hors d'oeuvre and drinks today.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Hors d'...? N-Never mind.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Well, I guess snacks are better than nothing.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Mm, this dessert ain't half bad... No wonder the girls always go for sweets when they're in a bad mood.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: It really does pick you right up.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Ooh, this cookie is great! If only it was bigger.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: And this mini burger... yum!

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Man, this cupcake is amazing!

steps.name: Arrogant Exhibition Guest
steps.text: This exhibition is going down the drain. Just look at the riff-raff you're letting in now.

steps.name: Aloof Exhibition Planner
steps.text: Who might you be referring to?

steps.name: Arrogant Exhibition Guest
steps.text: That man from the frontier processing station, of course. Who else?

steps.name: Aloof Exhibition Planner
steps.text: Oh, him... Did you see his display? I was too busy to visit.

steps.name: Arrogant Exhibition Guest
steps.text: I took a look. All scrap, not even worth my time.

steps.name: Aloof Exhibition Planner
steps.text: Figured as much, seeing how uncouth he is. Did you hear him yelling earlier? Nearly scared the daylights out of the other guests.

steps.name: Arrogant Exhibition Guest
steps.text: And look at him now, gorging on appetizers like he hasn't eaten in years.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Don't they even know to keep their voices down when trash talking someone behind their back?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Or I guess they don't even care what I think...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Well, whatever. Food comes first.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Hey, ain't that the reporter who wanted to interview me? Ma'am? Ma'am?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Looks like she's busy...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: At today's exhibition, the Cole Workshop took home four prizes for innovation and quality.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: This bracelet earned particular acclaim, winning Best Product in a unanimous decision.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Now, let us meet the inventor, Mrs. Yuria.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Best Product? This I gotta hear.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: What's with all these people? Are they all here to listen, too? Hey, stop pushing!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Can you tell us more about this bracelet, Mrs. Yuria?

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: Of course. This smart bracelet helps schools and parents keep track of children in real time.

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: It records various data, including movement, activity, health, and academic performance, etc.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: With all that, parents and teachers could even tell how many times the kids have gone to the bathroom.

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: Precisely.

steps.name: Investor
steps.text: That sounds like a wonderful product, helping parents understand what is going on with their child.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Ain't that just a monitoring bracelet?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: So what inspired you to invent this?

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: My own son closed himself off when he entered adolescence, refusing to tell us, his parents, what he was thinking.

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: So I invented this in order to get to know him better.

steps.name: Investor
steps.text: The very model of a responsible mother!

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: ...Responsible? That's just monitoring.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Are there any other, more general applications for the bracelet?

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: Of course. I have full confidence in that.

steps.name: Investor
steps.text: I could use that in my office. An employer should know what his employees are up to.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Are you kidding me, sir?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: It's just a goddamn monitoring bracelet!
Around Humus, people are talking excitedly about potential applications for the bracelet.
Their discussions drown out his voice.
And any who might have heard him paid no heed.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Vicious Soldier
steps.text: Get moving, people! Now put these on!

steps.name: Processing Station Prisoner
steps.text: (Whisper) What are they handing out?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Don't ask me. I was just working when they told me to come here.

steps.name: Processing Station Prisoner
steps.text: (Whisper) What were you up to this time?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) I made a gadget that can adjust how tight the shackles are, to make them a little comfier...

steps.name: Vicious Soldier
steps.text: Don't even think about running away once you've got these new shackles on. The moment the positioning tracker finds you're outside the station...

steps.name: Vicious Soldier
steps.text: Boom! There goes your leg. And don't even think about sabotaging them either, or else... kaboom!

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Well, I guess that was a waste of time.

steps.name: Vicious Soldier
steps.text: You dirtbags just keep your heads down and work your asses off. Don't even dream of slacking off either, 'cause these new shackles are gonna know.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: You're even putting those on a kid that young?

steps.name: Vicious Soldier
steps.text: Shut your trap!

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Ouch... This thing sure delivers a hella nasty electric shock...

steps.name: Skinny Boy
steps.text: Let's just go, mister. Don't say anything else.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Who are you calling mister? I'm not even twenty. The name's Humus.

steps.name: Skinny Boy
steps.text: Humus...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Don't you worry, I've got your back in this here station. I'm not letting any of the big guys bully you.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: But shit, they're sending kids like you here now?

steps.name: Skinny Boy
steps.text: Thanks, Humus.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: So how'd you end up here at your age?

steps.name: Skinny Boy
steps.text: Mom stole food and got caught...

steps.name: Skinny Boy
steps.text: But my little brother and sister need her... so I volunteered...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Well... let's get going. I'll have old Lippi arrange a bed for you. Can't have a kid like you sleeping on cardboard boxes like the rest of us dumbasses.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Man, I had to wait an hour for the guards to get off work.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Lemme check...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Yup, here it is.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Just a normal warehouse? Wasn't this place supposed to be cutting edge? No fingerprint lock, no password? All you need is a card.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Well, I should thank that dude for 'sharing' it. Hope he won't miss it much.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Now it's my turn.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Goddamn, are they even gonna have time to hand out all these awards at tomorrow's ceremony?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Most Innovative, Most Disruptive, Top 10 Hardcore Tech... ah, Best Product.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Let's see what's inside this baby...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Knew it. Almost the exact same thing as the shackles I used to wear.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: These people are outta their minds. They're gonna starting treating innocent kids like criminals now?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Not on my watch.
Under the dim moonlight, Humus reassembles the bracelet, then takes out an identical bracelet from his pocket.
The cold glint of metal stings his eyes.
He fiddles with the bracelets before putting one of them back on the shelf, and the other underneath it.
He looks to the sides and nods once satisfied that the bracelet underneath cannot be easily spotted. And then sighs.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: How could they treat innocent people like criminals?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: *Yawn* Did the awards ceremony have to be so early in the morning?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Well, I got you an appointment with another big shot who's also interested in your energy-saving module, and this guy has a reputation for being easy-going.

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Now, it is my pleasure to announce the winner of the Best Product award.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Sits up straight) Mm...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: What's that? You sure woke up in a hurry.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Shh, don't talk while they're talking!

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Mrs. Yuria, could you please step up and demonstrate your smart bracelet?

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: With all the distinguished inventors present, I'd be honored to.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Yeesh, why there gotta be so many people in front?

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: As you can see, we've gone with a minimalist style, despite the rich functionality of the product.

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: The goal is to reduce extraneous steps and allow for intuitive operation.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Come on, talk about that little button!

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: All it takes is the press of a button to open it...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Just press it already...

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: Hm? It's not responding...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Whoops, forgot it always takes a little smack to get my stuff working...

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: Maybe it ran out of batteries. Let me find my charging cord...
The woman tosses the bracelet onto the table and reaches into her bag for a cord, only to see the bracelet begin to bounce on the table.
Before she can react, it flies into the air and starts spraying colorful sparks in all directions.
The audience looks on, dumbfounded, as the bracelet continues to spin in the air and spit out fireworks.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: (Whisper) Come on, don't just watch...
Humus reaches into his pocket and pushes the remote control's slider up to max.
Orchestral music begins to play from the bracelet, and soon the hall is filled with a soaring soprano solo.
The members of the audience look at each other incredulously.

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: This isn't right... what's going on?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Yeah, that's not right... it's one of those hoity-toity songs Czerny recommended.

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: That's no good at all. Should be something funner.
Humus presses a button on his remote control.
The orchestra stops, replaced by a lively electronic dance tune.
♪Wave your left hand, hey, left hand♪
♪If you're feelin' the joy today♪
♪Shake your right foot, oh, right foot♪
♪Get drunk on this beautiful night♪

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Security! Grab that bracelet! What is the meaning of this, Mrs. Yuria?

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: I-I have no idea!

steps.name: Lanky Inventor
steps.text: Eek! It's flying towards me! Security!

steps.name: MC
steps.text: Just stay put! It's not moving! Hey! Hey!

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Hehe...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: What's so funny?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Look at all this chaos. Ain't it hilarious?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Well gee, I wonder whose fault this could be...?

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Haha, yeah... me too.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Still...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: While I can't say which of my coworkers did this, I can say that his taste in music is...

spans.text: While I can't say which of my coworkers did this, I
say that his taste in music is...

steps.name: Humus
steps.text: Top notch?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Engineer
steps.text: Abysmal!
